Content covers: the derivation that the phrase 'which the fire consumes of the burnt-offering' teaches about the end of the burning process (bits that pop off the fire) rather than its beginning, already covered elsewhere; the parallel derivation, via Rabbi Meir's own view, that only the burnt-offering's own remains, not the incense's own remains, are returned to the fire; the requirement that the fire for the Yom Kippur incense in the Holy of Holies and for the lampstand's own daily lighting must both be taken specifically from the outer altar, derived via a gezeirah shavah from the phrase 'fire' shared with the daily incense (itself taken from the inner altar, adjacent to the lampstand and the Holy of Holies); the identification of the 'perpetual fire' as the lampstand's own fire; and the extended derivation of which altar 'before the Lord' refers to, working through why the verse needed to specify 'from before the Lord' at all (since only the outer altar has a distinguishable part facing that direction, unlike the inner altar which is entirely so), narrowing 'before the Lord' to the specific western side directly opposite the entrance, closing into the daf-boundary comment that continues onto 46a.
